project.name: RescueStock
project.idea: Emergency purchasing assistant for small cafés: Arabic/English request and optional package image to structured requirements, exact supply plans over indivisible cup/lid bundles from demonstration suppliers, buyer approval, atomic inventory reservation, supplier confirmation, PayPal Sandbox authorize-then-capture per supplier with compensation, replanning when a supplier drops out. PayPal AI Hackathon entry built with ECCode 0.3.0.

lessons.title: A tool-call guard must resolve the project root from the target's real path, not from the harness's project directory, or nested projects are judged by the wrong record

lessonDecisions.note: Assessed does-not-apply by delivery-lead with ev:ev-mv1eo87o-01c933d5. The lesson is about a PreToolUse guard that resolves the project root from the harness directory; no task in this plan builds a hook or guard mapping writes to a record (the approved brief and spec name no such component), and the guard that governs this nested record is already the repaired version the lesson names (sha256 d43f4b54..., per-target fileRoot). It matches every task only through shared project words. Operational consequence kept in the plan anyway: every ownership glob is relative to examples/rescuestock and no glob names .eccode/, .claude/ or hooks.

acceptanceCriteria: RS-06: with RS-FIX-1 and the pinned inventory the planner returns A+B at 8400 cents, 2 pickups, ready 10:30; with A on_hand 2 it returns Ax2 at 7000 cents, 1 pickup; the oracle property test (500 seeded catalogs, <= 6 offers, on_hand 0-3) agrees with the planner on every catalog [D: test/unit/domain/planner-fixture.test.js, planner-oracle.property.test.js]
RS-07: supplier C is rejected with INCOMPATIBLE_LID_DIAMETER [D: planner-fixture]
RS-08: supplier D is rejected with READY_AFTER_DEADLINE [D: planner-fixture]
RS-09: with B at on_hand 0 and, separately, B withdrawn, the best plan is A+E at 9500 cents, 2 pickups, ready 10:40 [D: planner-fixture]

RS-10: B removed and budget 9000: infeasible, blocking includes OVER_BUDGET, A and E carry INSUFFICIENT_QTY and OVER_BUDGET, exactly two relaxations (budget -> 9500 A+E; deadline -> 11:20 D alone 8000, 1 pickup) and no maxPickups relaxation [D: planner-fixture]
RS-11: max pickups 1: infeasible; A, B and E carry exactly INSUFFICIENT_QTY and TOO_MANY_PICKUPS; C and D keep their RS-07/RS-08 codes [D: planner-fixture]

acceptanceCriteria: RS-12: a plan whose cups or lids total is below the requirement is never produced as feasible, and approve with a tampered planHash or expectedTotalCents returns 409 PLAN_CHANGED (stored plan failing re-validation: PLAN_INVALID) [D: test/api/approve-guards.test.js + planner-fixture]

RS-14: two OS processes (busy_timeout 5000) reserve A's last bundle concurrently on one SQLite file: one reservation active, the other 409 OUT_OF_STOCK, reserved <= on_hand; with busy_timeout 0 and a held write lock reserve answers 503 DB_BUSY with Retry-After [D: test/integration/rs14-two-process-reserve.test.js, rs14-db-busy.test.js]

RS-16: same Idempotency-Key and body -> same reservation id, no second reservation or ledger row; same key with another body -> 422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED; same key on a second plan -> 422 with no rows, before and after the key row is purged (F-TR-1); a concurrent same-key race resolves to one reservation [D: test/api/reserve-idempotency.test.js]
RS-28: supplier A patching supplier B's inventory gets 403 and nothing changes (whole PATCH refused) [D: test/api/isolation.test.js]
RS-30: customer and supplier sessions calling admin fault and reset routes get 403; unauthenticated 401 [D: test/api/isolation.test.js]

RS-33: browser journey at 360 px and 1280 px: an infeasible request ends on the explanation screen with blocking constraints, per-candidate codes and computed relaxations; no reservation, order or payment operation exists (checked in the database) [B: test/browser/journey-infeasible.test.js, screenshots in test/browser/out/]

phases.name: D: model extraction with provenance, uploads and retention
phases.goal: Bilingual extraction through the ExtractionProvider contract (deterministic fake for tests; Claude CLI and Anthropic API adapters verified against a recorded transcript and a loopback stub), strict schema validation, grounding and provenance, the degraded manual path, model budget/rate/concurrency controls in integer micro-dollars, image upload by magic bytes with retention and request deletion, the EXT-1 corpus and the opt-in live-model runner, and the matching UI.
acceptanceCriteria: RS-01 [D]: the RS-FIX-1 Arabic and English wordings yield identical core fields (product type, quantities, capacity, diameter, deadline, budget, max pickups) through POST /api/requests/:id/extract with the fake provider [test/api/extract.test.js]
RS-02 [D]: a clear package image yields capacity and diameter with provenance 'image' [test/api/extract-image.test.js]

RS-03 [D + B]: ambiguous images give unknown fields, >= 1 clarification question and no number absent from the image [test/eval/extraction-fake.test.js]; faults timeout, invalid_json, schema_invalid, error, budget refusal and rate refusal give schema_ok=false, an error code, every field unknown, degraded: true [test/api/extract-degraded.test.js]; the request page shows 'Automatic reading unavailable — please enter the details' with a manual field for every core field, and confirming them creates a requirements version with provenance manual and planning proceeds [test/browser/degraded-extraction.test.js]

RS-05 [D]: injection strings in text, image text and catalog text (planted in products.name through a DB fixture, SEC-17) stay data; permissions, amounts, suppliers, plan versions and roles equal the control run; explanations are template text; with rephrasing on, output carrying a number or supplier code absent from the trace is discarded [test/api/injection.test.js, test/unit/ai/rephrase.test.js]

RS-39 [D]: upload accepts only PNG/JPEG/WebP by magic bytes (declared image/png with other bytes -> 415), <= 5 MB (413 above), stored under a random 128-bit name; customer Y uploading to X's request -> 404 with no file written; owner DELETE removes image file and row, raw text and extraction text (409 PAYMENT_IN_PROGRESS while money is held; tombstone with settled payments); with a pinned clock the sweep deletes at 7 d + 1 min, keeps at 6 d 23 h and writes an audit event [test/api/uploads-retention.test.js]

NFR6 [D]: every response and log line carries requestId; config inspection shows haiku as the default model; with fake per-call cost 0.10, cap 0.10, RS_MODEL_DAILY_BUDGET_USD=0.25 and RS_MODEL_CUSTOMER_DAILY_SHARE=1 pinned in the test's environment (F-TR-18; the test name and the evidence label say so) the third extract is refused with 503 MODEL_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED without invoking the provider and enters the degraded path; the 11th extract or upload by one customer within 10 minutes -> 429 RATE_LIMITED with Retry-After; micro-dollar boundaries (0.30 allowed, 0.299999 refused) hold; a separate SEC-10 case with the production share 0.2 refuses the 5th cap-sized call of one customer with details.scope 'customer' while another customer succeeds [test/api/model-budget-rate.test.js]; the log scan finds no Authorization header value, token, secret, payer data or provider body [test/scan/secrets.test.js]

Live-model parts are not claimed by this phase: npm run test:live-model refuses (exit 2, named message) without RS_LIVE_MODEL=1 [D]; the real-model run over EXT-1 (RS-01/02/03/05 [LM], NFR6 cost report, F-TR-13 schemaAccepted) is the separately listed check LIVE-M1 and stays Unverified until it is run with an authenticated Claude CLI or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and the user's approval of the USD 5 ceiling
ExtractionProvider contract suite (fake, CLI against a stub binary replaying the recorded transcript, Anthropic against a loopback stub) passes [test/unit/ai/provider-contract.test.js]

phases.name: E: PayPal payment flow, saga, webhooks and reconciliation
phases.goal: The PaymentProvider contract with a DB-backed fake (faults, PayPal-Request-Id replay model, fake approval listener on a different site with its own CSP) and the Sandbox REST v2 adapter verified against a loopback paypal-stub; the provider call protocol with the sender table; create/return/cancel/abandon with the void rule; the execute claim and captures with lease fencing; the reconciler (stale intents, read-before-resend, pending polls, expiry); verified webhooks; the payment UI; and the two-process execute and browser happy-path journeys.
acceptanceCriteria: RS-04: with budget or deadline missing, POST /api/plans/:id/approve and POST /api/orders/:id/paypal/create return 409 MISSING_BUDGET / MISSING_DEADLINE (budget first) and no reservation or payment operation or provider call is created [D: test/api/approve-guards.test.js, test/api/paypal-create.test.js]

RS-18 [D]: cancel URL leaves the operation created with buyer_cancelled_at (or voided), no capture call or row, execute -> 409; 'Try approval again' and 'Abandon purchase' offered; abandon or expiry voids every other outstanding authorization, releases the reservation, plan non_executable (PAYMENT_CANCELLED or RESERVATION_EXPIRED) [test/api/paypal-cancel.test.js]

RS-19 [D]: client-supplied amount, currency or supplier on every payment route is ignored; the provider request body (fake and Sandbox adapter against paypal-stub) carries the server-approved supplier-order total [test/api/amount-tampering.test.js]

RS-20 [D]: two server processes x 5 concurrent execute: one approved -> executing claim, nine return the current state with no provider call; the fake records exactly N get_authorization + N capture calls and nothing else (F-TR-8), one capture per order with PayPal-Request-Id so:<id>:capture:1; three hits on the return URL give one authorize call [test/integration/rs20-two-process-execute.test.js, test/api/paypal-return-idempotent.test.js]

RS-21 [D]: one DENIED authorization -> no capture on any order, plan non_executable (AUTHORIZATION_FAILED naming the supplier), other authorizations voided, reservation released, the exact buyer message; PENDING -> authorization_pending and execute 409 AUTHORIZATION_PENDING with no capture until the reconciler observes CREATED [test/api/authorization-denied.test.js, test/api/authorization-pending.test.js]

RS-23 [D]: the same webhook transmission id delivered twice applies once; RS-24 [D]: an invalid signature is rejected 4xx, stored with signature_status invalid, no transition; plus SEC-6 (60/min per IP, pre-checks before any provider call) and SEC-16 (merchant, provider and non-archived scoping) [test/api/webhooks.test.js]

RS-25 [D]: a lost capture response leaves the operation unknown; the reconciler reads provider state and then marks captured, capture_pending (polled) or re-sends with the same PayPal-Request-Id; no second capture; an intent left at restart is treated as unknown [test/api/lost-response.test.js]

RS-27 [D]: customer X requesting Y's request or order id gets 404/403 and no data, including /api/paypal/return?token= and /cancel?token= with Y's token (404, no authorize call, no state change) [test/api/isolation.test.js]

RS-31(a) [B]: journey request -> review -> plan -> reservation -> approvals -> supplier confirmations -> capture -> readiness -> collection at 360 px and 1280 px with screenshots, the app on localhost and the fake approval page on 127.0.0.1 (cross-site), each 'Approve (simulated)' landing on /api/paypal/return with the session, one Cancel landing on /api/paypal/cancel, no CSP console message (F-TR-14) [test/browser/journey-happy.test.js]; the listener and paypal-stub send exactly one CSP header equal to approvalPageCsp(appOrigin) [D: test/api/fake-approval-headers.test.js]

Design items asserted: ARCH-22 lost-authorize void hook (test/api/void-rule-lost-authorize.test.js), ARCH-23 claim on stored expiry with the provider read after the claim (test/api/execute.test.js), F-TR-3 sender table and crash_after_return_commit hook implemented, F-TR-11 order presentation, SEC-3 approval-host and base-URL allow-list in the Sandbox adapter, PaymentProvider contract suite on both adapters (test/unit/payments/provider-contract.test.js)

Live PayPal parts are not claimed by this phase: npm run test:live-paypal refuses without RS_LIVE_PAYPAL=1 and credentials; the Sandbox runs (LIVE-P1: RS-18/19/20/23/24 [LP]; LIVE-P2: RS-31(b)/RS-32(b) hosted approval page) need RS_PAYPAL_DEFAULT_CLIENT_ID, RS_PAYPAL_DEFAULT_CLIENT_SECRET, RS_PAYPAL_DEFAULT_WEBHOOK_ID (or per-supplier sets) and network access to api-m.sandbox.paypal.com and www.sandbox.paypal.com, are user-run, and stay Unverified with blocker A6/Q2 until then
npm test and npm run test:browser pass

phases.name: F: replanning, compensation and restart recovery
phases.goal: Supersession on offer and stock changes with the durable re-plan queue, supplier refusal with re-planning that excludes the supplier, expiry voids, capture-failure compensation (voids, refunds, reconciling -> released with restock), lease takeover with epoch and send-token fencing, restart recovery, admin refund_order and forced reset, ledger completeness, the recovery UI, and the restart, takeover and replacement-journey tests.
acceptanceCriteria: RS-13 [D]: a price change of an offer used by an approved plan (order not confirmed, plan not executing) supersedes it, recomputes a new proposed version, reserve/execute on the old one -> 409 PLAN_SUPERSEDED, every old authorization voided (one void call each), reservation released (one ledger row per item), orders cancelled, 'Prices changed: review plan vN' shown; after the supplier confirmed or after the claim the plan is not superseded [test/api/supersession.test.js]

RS-15 [D]: an expired reservation is released exactly once (inventory back, one expire ledger row, second pass no-op); an expiry pass after the claim and before the first capture changes nothing; expiry before execute voids every authorization, plan non_executable (RESERVATION_EXPIRED) and the request shows 'Reservation expired — no money was taken; re-plan with current stock' [test/api/reservation-expiry.test.js]

RS-17 [D + B]: refusal before the claim -> order refused, outstanding authorizations voided, reservation released, plan non_executable (SUPPLIER_REFUSED), status cancelling while a void is outstanding, refusal reason with 'Review the new plan', new version computed without that supplier [test/api/supplier-refusal.test.js; test/browser/refusal.test.js]

RS-22 [D]: capture failing on the second supplier refunds the first capture and voids the rest; refund_requested -> refund_pending -> refunded|refund_failed; plan non_executable (CAPTURE_FAILED); reservation reconciling until every refund and void completes, then released with restock rows (refund_failed keeps reconciling and failed_needs_attention); handover 409 HANDOVER_BLOCKED; a PENDING capture blocks handover and the next capture, and lease_epoch does not grow across reconciler ticks while it is pending (F-TR-7) [test/api/capture-compensation.test.js]

RS-26 [D]: SIGKILL mid-saga and restart keeps orders, operations, provider calls and recovery progress; after the lease expires the reconciler takes over and completes the saga; lease-takeover variants A and B (ARCH-26) give exactly one non-replayed capture per order; return-crash cases (a), (b), (c) (F-TR-3) [test/integration/rs26-restart.test.js, lease-takeover.test.js, return-crash.test.js]

RS-32(a) [B]: B's offer withdrawn by the admin stock-depletion fault before B confirms; the buyer approves the 9500-cent A+E plan; the old plan superseded, its authorizations voided, B's order cancelled; the replacement flow completes through collection with the cross-site approval round-trip assertion [test/browser/journey-replacement.test.js]

RS-37 [D]: admin reset returns 409 RESET_BLOCKED while any operation is approved|authorization_pending|authorized|capture_pending|captured|refund_requested|refund_pending|unknown; forced reset requires a reason, voids authorized operations and runs one bounded read-resolve pass, lists stranded operations (SEC-11), and archives rather than deletes operations and provider calls [test/api/admin-reset.test.js]

RS-38 [D]: any UPDATE or DELETE on audit_events or inventory_ledger fails; every reserve, release, expire, consume and restock writes a ledger row, and for every product the ledger sums equal on_hand and reserved [test/api/ledgers.test.js]

Design items asserted: F-TR-2 re-plan queue never drops an entry and backs off (test/api/replan-queue.test.js); F-TR-6 capture landing after the void intent ends refunded with one capture, one void attempt and one refund call (test/api/void-capture-race.test.js)

rev-mv16o544-0127ccbf.summary: Independent review of submission sub-mv15wpmr-015f7530 (brief.md only). The brief is well structured: all 45 required ids are present with test-suite tags, the trust boundaries are explicit, each major choice is weighed against an alternative, and the risk register has owners. Seven major findings block approval. (1) The fixture does not pin inventory. My brute force (ev:ev-mv16ez5r-01e792ff) shows that RS-06/09/10/11 hold only when A, B and E each have exactly one bundle on hand. With A at 2 bundles, the planner the brief adopts returns A x2 = 7000 cents with 1 pickup. (2) The honest-status model has no provider PENDING outcome and no derivation rule for the aggregate rescue status. (3) Execute has no stated exclusive claim. Nothing guards against reservation expiry during execute, and outstanding authorizations are never voided on supersession, refusal, authorization failure or cancel. (4) RS-34 narrows the goal's labelling scope. (5) NFR1 cannot be met as written: node:sqlite needs a flag on Node 22.5-22.12 and the browser suites have no script. (6) RS-31/32 replace the PayPal approval with the fake adapter page. (19) The architecture section delegates modules, data model, planner and saga to the unsubmitted docs/build/plan.md, and the fixture table exists only in docs/build/goal.md. Minor and info findings follow. The previous unrecorded draft was checked claim by claim. Its 18 findings were substantiated and kept, with ARCH-8 downgraded to info and ARCH-16 raised to minor. ARCH-19 to ARCH-21 are new.

criteria.description: Equivalent Arabic and English requests (RS-FIX-1 wording) yield identical core fields: product type, quantities, capacity, diameter, deadline, budget, max pickups. [D with fake provider; LM with real model, equality on normalised fields]
criteria.notes: Decidable by equality on normalised fields. Covered by the AI feature statement's eval set (>= 10 bilingual requests, >= 90 % field match).

criteria.description: A clear package image yields capacity/diameter specifications carrying `provenance: "image"`. [D fake; LM real]
An ambiguous image yields `unknown` for unreadable fields plus at least one clarification question, and no numeric value absent from the image. [D fake; LM real]

With budget or deadline missing, `POST /api/plans/:id/approve` and `POST /api/orders/:id/paypal/create` return 409 with a named reason (`MISSING_BUDGET` / `MISSING_DEADLINE`) and no reservation or payment operation is created. [D]
criteria.notes: Testing the paypal/create path needs a seeded order, because an approval refused for missing fields creates no order. The design should name that fixture.

criteria.description: Injection strings in image text and catalog text appear only as data in `fields_json`/catalog; after extraction no permission, amount, supplier, plan version or role differs from the control run. [D fake with injection fixtures; LM real]
criteria.notes: The control run must also cover the explain.js rephrasing path (ARCH-13).

criteria.description: Canonical RS-FIX-1 returns plan A+B with total 8400 cents, 2 pickups, ready 10:30. [D]
criteria.notes: Holds only if A and B each have one bundle on hand. With A at 2 bundles the result is A x2 = 7000 cents (ARCH-1). The fixture table is not in the brief (ARCH-19).

criteria.description: Supplier C's bundle is listed under rejections with code `INCOMPATIBLE_LID_DIAMETER`. [D]
criteria.notes: Independent of inventory: C is rejected in every scenario of the brute force.

criteria.description: Supplier D's bundle is rejected with code `READY_AFTER_DEADLINE`. [D]
With B removed (out of stock or offer withdrawn) the best plan is A+E at 9500 cents. [D]
criteria.notes: Inventory-dependent, like RS-06 (ARCH-1).

criteria.description: With B removed and budget 9000 cents the planner returns no feasible plan, lists the blocking constraints (`OVER_BUDGET`) and at least one suggestion (raise budget to 9500, allow later ready time, or more pickups). [D]
criteria.notes: Inventory-dependent (ARCH-1). The 'more pickups' suggestion does not produce a plan (ARCH-7).

criteria.description: With max pickups = 1 the canonical scenario is infeasible with `TOO_MANY_PICKUPS`/`INSUFFICIENT_QTY` explanations per candidate. [D]
criteria.notes: Becomes feasible if A, B or E has 2 bundles (ARCH-1).

criteria.description: A plan whose cups or lids total < required quantity cannot be produced as feasible, and approval of a tampered plan body is refused with 409. [D]

After an offer price changes, the approved plan version becomes `superseded`, totals are recalculated in a new version, and reserve/execute on the old version is refused until the new version is approved. [D]
criteria.notes: The brief does not say when supersession stops applying (after supplier commitment or capture), or what happens to authorizations already held at the old amount (ARCH-3).

criteria.description: Two separate OS processes reserve the last bundle concurrently against the same SQLite file; exactly one reservation is `active`, the other receives `OUT_OF_STOCK`; `reserved <= on_hand` holds. [D, multi-process]
criteria.notes: Feasible, but only with a busy timeout. With the node:sqlite default of 0 the losing process gets 'database is locked', not OUT_OF_STOCK (ARCH-20). 'Last bundle' depends on the unpinned inventory (ARCH-1).

criteria.description: An expired reservation is released exactly once: inventory returns to its prior value, the ledger holds one release row, and a second expiry pass is a no-op. [D]
criteria.notes: The AC is decidable. The interaction between expiry and execute is raised under ARCH-3(b).

criteria.description: Two `reserve` calls with the same `Idempotency-Key` return the same reservation id and create no second reservation or ledger row. [D]
criteria.notes: The design should refuse the same key with a different body (ARCH-14).

criteria.description: Supplier refusal sets the order to `refused`, the customer request shows the refusal with next step, and a new plan version is computed excluding that supplier. [D; B]
criteria.notes: The fate of the other suppliers' authorizations and reservation items after a refusal is not specified (ARCH-3c).

criteria.description: Cancelling on PayPal (cancel URL) leaves the operation `voided`/`created`, no capture row exists, and `execute` refuses. [D fake; LP]
criteria.notes: When one supplier's approval is cancelled, the other suppliers' authorizations are not voided (ARCH-3c). Return/cancel handling has no ownership rule, and the reused cookie pattern is SameSite=Strict (ARCH-10).

criteria.description: A client-supplied amount/currency/supplier on any payment route is ignored; the PayPal order amount equals the server-approved plan total. [D; LP]
N concurrent or repeated `execute` requests produce exactly one capture per supplier order (operation key unique, `PayPal-Request-Id` reused). [D fake; LP]
criteria.notes: No deterministic key derivation or exclusive claim is stated. PayPal-Request-Id retention is unverified (ARCH-3a).

criteria.description: If one supplier's authorization fails, no capture occurs on any supplier order and the plan is `non_executable` with reason. [D]
criteria.notes: The surviving authorizations are left open (no void), so the buyer's funds stay held (ARCH-3c).

criteria.description: With capture failing on the second supplier, the first capture is refunded, uncaptured authorizations voided, statuses read `refund_requested → refund_pending → refunded|refund_failed`, reservation `reconciling`, handover blocked. [D fake faults]
criteria.notes: No state for a provider capture or authorization PENDING outcome (ARCH-2a).

criteria.description: Delivering the same webhook (same transmission id) twice applies its effect once. [D; LP]
A webhook with an invalid signature is rejected (4xx), recorded with `signature_status: invalid`, and applies no transition. [D; LP]
After a simulated lost response on capture, the operation is `unknown`; the reconciler fetches provider state and only then marks `captured` or retries; no second capture. [D fake]
criteria.notes: The reconciler may fetch a provider state of PENDING, which the brief cannot represent. The AC does not say what the reconciler does then (ARCH-2a).

criteria.description: Killing and restarting the server mid-saga preserves orders, payment operations and recovery progress; the reconciler completes the saga. [D]
Customer X requesting customer Y's request or order id receives 404/403 and no data. [D]
Supplier A patching supplier B's inventory receives 403 and B's inventory is unchanged. [D]
A scan of built frontend assets, API responses, logs, screenshots and submission files finds no client id/secret value; config redacts secrets in errors. [D scan; I]
Customer and supplier sessions calling admin fault/reset routes receive 403; unauthenticated 401. [D]
Browser journey at 360 px and 1280 px: request → review → plan → reservation → PayPal approvals (fake adapter page) → supplier confirmations → capture → readiness → collection, with screenshots. [B]
criteria.notes: The goal's 'PayPal approvals' is narrowed to the fake adapter page (ARCH-6). No script runs [B] suites (ARCH-5).

criteria.description: Browser journey: B becomes unavailable after approval; buyer reviews and approves the $95 plan; old plan `superseded`; replacement flow completes. [B]
criteria.notes: Same narrowing as RS-31 (ARCH-6). The $95 outcome depends on pinned inventory (ARCH-1).

criteria.description: Browser journey: an infeasible request ends on an explanation screen with blocking constraints and suggestions; no reservation, order or payment operation exists. [B]
criteria.notes: The suggestions must be computed relaxations (ARCH-7).

criteria.description: API payloads from fake adapters carry `"simulated": true`; UI shows provider badges and a persistent banner while a fake adapter is active. [D; B]
criteria.notes: Narrower than the goal: Sandbox transactions and demonstration data are not labelled (ARCH-4).

criteria.description: The request page shows all six answers (requirements with provenance, decision trace, rejections, cents totals, offer vs commitment, compensation state). [B; I]
State tables persist plan, reservation, payment operation and fulfilment statuses separately; the rescue status endpoint is computed and has no stored column. [D; I]
criteria.notes: There is no derivation rule. The goal's aggregate states cancelling, refunding and failed_needs_attention do not appear in the brief (ARCH-2b).

criteria.description: Admin reset returns 409 while any payment operation is `authorized|captured|refund_pending|unknown`; forced reset records a reason and archives rather than deletes payment operations. [D]
criteria.notes: Extend the guard list with any pending states added under ARCH-2.

criteria.description: Any UPDATE/DELETE on `audit_events` or `inventory_ledger` fails; every reservation/release/consume writes a ledger row. [D]
Upload rejects >5 MB and non-PNG/JPEG/WebP; stored name is random; deletion with the request is verified. [D]
criteria.notes: Type check basis and owner check are unspecified (ARCH-17). The 7-day deletion is untested and depends on a manual admin reset (ARCH-21).

criteria.description: A clean clone on Node ≥ 22.5 runs `npm test` and the server from the README with no network beyond npm; `package.json` has no `dependencies`. [D; I]
criteria.notes: node:sqlite is behind --experimental-sqlite on 22.5-22.12. Playwright browsers are not an npm download (ARCH-5).

criteria.description: Playwright checks at 360 px and 1280 px: keyboard-only completion of the happy path, visible focus, labelled controls, text status indicators; loading/empty/error/retry/timeout/expired-reservation states rendered. [B]
criteria.notes: Decidable. The script placement is raised under ARCH-5.

criteria.description: `npm test` (deterministic), `npm run test:live-model` (`RS_LIVE_MODEL=1`) and `npm run test:live-paypal` (`RS_LIVE_PAYPAL=1`) are separate scripts; live reports are labelled. [I]
criteria.notes: The live suites are separated as the goal requires. A browser script is still missing (ARCH-5).

criteria.description: Config reads secrets only from `process.env`; `.env.example` contains names and placeholders only; a test asserts no real-looking value. [D; I]
Planner on RS-FIX-1 and random catalogs ≤ 12 offers completes < 1 s; deterministic suite < 5 min offline. [D timing]
criteria.notes: The random-catalog distribution is undefined. The requirement's API p95 < 300 ms has no AC (ARCH-9).

criteria.description: Every response and log line carries `requestId`; live model run cost is reported and ≤ USD 1. [D; LM report]
criteria.notes: The 'logs never contain secrets or raw payloads' clause is untested (ARCH-9). There is no runtime spend ceiling (ARCH-11).

criteria.description: Users, problems, workflows, constraints and scope are explicit; no missing authz, retention, error handling, accessibility, observability, abuse or cost requirements
criteria.notes: Users, scope and workflows are explicit. Gaps: aggregate status derivation (ARCH-2), authorization lifecycle (ARCH-3), runtime abuse/cost (ARCH-11), retention (ARCH-21), core design delegated to an unsubmitted file (ARCH-19).

criteria.description: Each acceptance criterion is decidable by test or inspection and every requirement traces to a criterion
criteria.notes: Traceability is 1:1 for all 45 ids. RS-06/09/10/11 are undecidable without pinned inventory. NFR5/NFR6 clauses lack ACs. The [B] suites have no script.

criteria.description: Risky or false assumptions identified; open questions that block design are listed with the decision they block
criteria.notes: A2 and A10 are unverified against primary sources (ARCH-18). Q1/Q3/Q6 have workable defaults (ARCH-15).

criteria.description: No unnecessary component; simplest design that meets the requirements
criteria.notes: Single process, SQLite, stateful fake adapter: proportionate. The model rephrasing of explanations is optional surface (ARCH-13).

criteria.description: Technology limits, rate limits, latency and cost are feasible
criteria.notes: node:sqlite version and flag (ARCH-5). Busy timeout (ARCH-20). nodejs.org/api/sqlite.html checked 2026-10-09.

criteria.description: Trust boundaries, secrets, PII, prompt injection and least privilege addressed
criteria.notes: The trust boundaries are sound. Gaps: return-URL ownership and cookie SameSite (ARCH-10), upload magic bytes and owner check (ARCH-17), PII retention (ARCH-21).

criteria.description: AI adds real value; evaluation cases with thresholds; fallback when the model fails; human oversight
criteria.notes: Value, thresholds and human-in-the-loop are present. The runtime degraded path and the eval corpus location are missing (ARCH-12).

criteria.description: Risk register has likelihood, impact, mitigation and owner for every material risk
criteria.notes: RISK-1..12 are complete. Missing: authorization expiry before capture, browser install on clean clones, experimental node:sqlite (ARCH-16).

findings.title: RS-FIX-1 does not pin inventory, so RS-06/09/10/11 hold only under an unstated one-bundle assumption
findings.detail: The brief adopts plan.md section 5 unchanged. That planner enumerates multiplicities 0..ceil(N/qty) per offer, bounded by availability = on_hand - reserved. Neither the brief nor goal.md's RS-FIX-1 table gives on_hand per supplier. In the brief, on_hand occurs only in RS-14 and RISK-4 (ev:ev-mv16g60f-0190c7f8). My brute-force lexicographic solver over the fixture (ev:ev-mv16ez5r-01e792ff) reproduces every expected outcome with one bundle per supplier: A+B 8400 / 2 pickups / 10:30; without B, A+E 9500; without B at 9000, no plan; max 1 pickup, no plan. With A at 2 bundles it returns A x2 = 7000 cents, 1 pickup, which also makes max-pickups-1 feasible. With B at 2 it returns B x2 = 8000. With E at 2, max-pickups-1 becomes feasible at E x2 = 10000. Of all 27 inventories (A, B, E in 0..2), only A=1, B=1, E=1 satisfies RS-06, RS-09, RS-10 and RS-11 together. The oracle property test (<= 6 offers) as described also does not require catalogs with multiplicity > 1.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the brief states the fixture inventory: on_hand = 1 bundle for each of A-E, or offers declared as single-unit 'take it or leave it' lots. RS-06/09/10/11 and RS-14's 'last bundle' must reference it, the seed must load it, and the oracle property test must include catalogs with on_hand >= 2 so that multiplicity is exercised.

findings.title: Honest statuses incomplete: no provider PENDING outcome and no derivation rule for the aggregate rescue status
findings.detail: (a) The project's own integration research (ev:ev-mv16gcdz-01d03c53, marked 'verify'; paypal.com is blocked here, so not re-checked) lists authorization status PENDING and capture status PENDING as provider outcomes. The brief's payment machine (RS-22, RS-25, Workflows 4 and 6) has no such state. A pending capture would have to be shown as captured (false), failed (false) or unknown. But unknown is reserved for lost responses, and the reconciler would then 'resolve' it to a provider state that is still pending. (b) goal.md defines the rescue aggregate, including cancelling, refunding and failed_needs_attention, as derived and never stored. The brief contains none of those three state names (ev:ev-mv16g60f-0190c7f8). RS-36's AC only checks that no stored column exists. An implementation that reports purchase_confirmed while a supplier order is refused, or a refund is pending, would therefore pass.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the brief does all three of the following. (a) Adds explicit pending states (e.g. authorization_pending, capture_pending) with their allowed transitions and reconciler polling, plus the rule that capture never starts from authorization_pending and handover stays blocked while capture_pending; RS-22/RS-25 must name these states. (b) Includes a derivation table from the plan/reservation/payment/fulfilment states to every goal aggregate state, with precedence. (c) Extends RS-36's AC with at least three derivation assertions: any refund_requested/refund_pending gives refunding; a refusal or non_executable with outstanding money gives cancelling or failed_needs_attention as defined; collected only when every supplier order is collected and every capture is completed.

findings.title: Execute lacks an exclusive claim, nothing guards against reservation expiry during capture, and authorizations are never voided outside the capture-failure path
findings.detail: (a) RS-20 relies on 'operation key unique', but the brief never says how the capture operation key is derived. If it is generated per request, two concurrent execute calls (or two processes, which RS-14 already assumes exist) can both pass revalidation and both capture. The PayPal-Request-Id backstop has unverified retention (ev:ev-mv16gcdz-01d03c53), and the fake adapter does not model it. (b) Workflow 6 revalidates 'reservation active' and then captures sequentially. Nothing stops the expiry job from releasing the reservation in between, which would leave a capture against released stock. (c) Void appears only in the capture-phase compensation (Workflow 6, RS-22). The brief does not say what happens to outstanding authorizations, or what the buyer sees, in five cases: RS-21 (one authorization failed, the others stay open), RS-17 (supplier refusal after authorization), RS-13 (plan superseded after authorization at the old amount), reservation expiry, and RS-18 (one supplier's approval cancelled while another is already authorized). RS-13 also does not say when supersession stops applying (after supplier commitment, after capture).
findings.recommendation: Resolved when Workflow 6 and the ACs state four things. (1) The claim mechanism: a deterministic capture operation_key per (supplier order, kind) inserted inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE as the claim, or a plan approved -> executing transition, with RS-20 extended to two OS processes. (2) The reservation is moved to consumed (or marked in-flight) in the same transaction, before the first capture call, with an AC that an expiry pass during execute is a no-op. (3) For RS-13, RS-17, RS-18, RS-21 and expiry: all outstanding authorizations are voided, end in status voided, and the buyer sees a stated next step, with assertions added to those ACs. (4) The point after which a price change no longer supersedes the plan.

findings.title: RS-34 narrows the goal's labelling requirement to fake adapters only
findings.detail: goal.md: 'All demonstration data, simulations, test providers and Sandbox transactions are labelled in the UI and the API'. The brief's RS-34 and its AC cover only payloads and UI from fake adapters (ev:ev-mv16g60f-0190c7f8). Real Sandbox payments and the seeded suppliers A-E with their 'test prices, not market prices' (the phrase does not occur in the brief) are left unlabelled. This weakens a mandatory scope statement, although the brief says requirements are kept unweakened.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when RS-34 and its AC also require three things, tested [D; B] for both adapters: real-adapter payment payloads and UI carry a provider marker (e.g. provider: 'paypal-sandbox') and a visible 'Sandbox - no real money' badge; seeded suppliers, offers and prices carry a demonstration flag that the UI renders; and the 'test prices, not market prices' notice is shown.

findings.title: NFR1 cannot be met as written: node:sqlite is flagged on Node 22.5-22.12, and the browser suites have no script
findings.detail: (a) nodejs.org/api/sqlite.html (checked 2026-10-09) gives the module history: node:sqlite was added in v22.5.0 behind --experimental-sqlite and unflagged in v22.13.0/v23.4.0. The DatabaseSync timeout option arrived in v22.16.0. So a clean clone on Node 22.5-22.12 that runs plain `node` cannot load the database. The brief's Constraints only record Node 22.22 here. ev:ev-mv16frja-017d17a4 shows the flag is still accepted on 22.22, so passing it in scripts is safe. (b) The [B] Playwright suites (RS-17, RS-31..35, NFR2) are assigned to no script. NFR3 lists only npm test and the two live scripts (ev:ev-mv16g60f-0190c7f8). If [B] runs under npm test, a clean clone must download Chromium from Playwright's CDN, which is network beyond npm. The brief notes that Chromium is pre-installed only in this build environment.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the brief does two things. First, it states how node:sqlite loads on every supported version: either npm scripts and the README start command pass --experimental-sqlite (and set the busy timeout via PRAGMA, since the constructor option needs 22.16), or the user approves raising the floor to Node >= 22.13. Second, it defines the script layout: npm test = deterministic node --test only, offline after npm install; npm run test:browser = Playwright, with the one-time browser install documented in the README. NFR1's AC must be phrased against npm test, and the [B] ACs must name test:browser.

findings.title: RS-31/RS-32 replace the user's 'PayPal approvals' with the fake adapter page instead of marking the live variant Unverified
findings.detail: goal.md RS-31: 'Request -> review -> plan -> reservation -> PayPal approvals -> ...'. Its preamble says requirement text is not weakened, and that criteria needing an unreachable integration are marked Unverified with the blocker. The brief's RS-31 reads 'PayPal approvals (fake adapter page)' [B] only (ev:ev-mv16g60f-0190c7f8). RS-32 likewise names only [B]. The Success Criteria extend Sandbox evidence only to RS-18..26. The end-to-end journey through PayPal's hosted Sandbox approval page is the central demonstration for a PayPal hackathon. It is also the only path that would reveal the cross-site return problem in ARCH-10.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when RS-31 and RS-32 each carry two variants. The first is [B fake], deterministic here. The second is [LP, user-run]: through the real Sandbox hosted approval page, with screenshots, recorded as Unverified with blocker A6/Q2 until the user runs it. The Success Criteria must also state that the demo video uses the Sandbox approval page.

findings.title: RS-10's example suggestions include a relaxation that does not yield a plan
findings.detail: For the scenario without B at budget 9000, the brute force (ev:ev-mv16ez5r-01e792ff) gives these results. Budget raised to 9500: A+E at 9500. Deadline moved to 11:20: D alone at 8000. Max pickups 3 or 5: still no plan. A planner that emits 'more pickups' would pass the AC while giving the buyer wrong advice.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when suggestions are defined as computed relaxations, each naming the relaxed constraint and the plan and total it yields (budget 9500 -> A+E; deadline 11:20 -> D at 8000). RS-10 must assert those two values and drop 'more pickups' from its example list.

findings.title: NFR1..4 alias for RS-NF-1..4 is forced by the engine; keep the mapping visible downstream
findings.detail: lib/gates.js:197 defines CRITERION_ID = /^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*-?\d+$/. That pattern accepts RS-01 and NFR1 and rejects RS-NF-1 (ev:ev-mv16ggcp-011ee455), so the alias is necessary. The texts are semantically unchanged and the user's ids are kept in parentheses.
findings.recommendation: Add the NFR1..4 = RS-NF-1..4 mapping to docs/build/evidence.md and the acceptance-report template.

findings.title: NFR5/NFR6 requirement text promises more than the ACs test; NFR5's random catalog is undefined
findings.detail: The NFR5 requirement includes 'API p95 < 300 ms'. The NFR6 requirement includes 'logs never contain secrets or raw card/PayPal payloads beyond ids' and 'haiku by default'. Neither AC includes these clauses. NFR5's 'random catalogs <= 12 offers' gives no bounds on bundle sizes or quantities. With multiplicity 0..ceil(N/qty), a catalog of 10-unit offers is exponentially larger than RS-FIX-1, so the < 1 s criterion is not decidable until the generator is defined.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the NFR5 AC defines the generator (offer count, quantity and availability bounds, seed) and includes or drops the p95 clause, and the NFR6 AC includes or drops the log-content scan (which can share the RS-29 scan).

findings.title: PayPal return/cancel handling: token ownership, idempotent authorize, and a session cookie that will not survive the cross-site return
findings.detail: Workflow 4 authorizes when PayPal redirects back to the return URL. The brief does not say that the token must resolve to a payment operation owned by the session's customer. Nor does it say that repeated return hits (refresh, back button) authorize at most once. RS-20 covers capture only. plan.md says Groundwork's session patterns are reused, and Groundwork sets the session cookie with SameSite=Strict (ev:ev-mv16ggcp-011ee455). Browsers do not send Strict cookies on the top-level navigation back from www.sandbox.paypal.com, so the return handler would see no session. The fake adapter page is same-origin, so every deterministic and [B] test would still pass.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the brief or design states four things. (1) The return/cancel handler looks the token up by provider_order_id and checks owner scope (404 otherwise). (2) Authorize is keyed per supplier order and idempotent. (3) The session cookie is SameSite=Lax, or the return handler authenticates by token and then redirects same-site. (4) The fake adapter's approval page is served from a different origin in [B] tests, or the live variant (ARCH-6) covers the return. A repeated-return assertion must be added to RS-18 or RS-20.

findings.title: No runtime spend ceiling or rate limit on customer-triggered paid model calls
findings.detail: NFR6's USD 1 ceiling applies to the live test suite. At runtime, extract and image upload trigger paid model calls with only per-call caps. 'Rate limit' does not occur in the brief (ev:ev-mv16g60f-0190c7f8). A customer looping extract can spend without bound, billed to the user's account (A4).
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the brief adds a configurable daily model budget, after which the provider refuses with a labelled error, plus a per-session rate limit on extract and image upload, each with a deterministic AC.

findings.title: No runtime degraded path when the real model fails; eval corpus location unspecified
findings.detail: The AI feature statement covers test doubles, caps and quality thresholds. It does not say what the customer experiences when the real provider times out or returns schema-invalid output; the fake provider is a test double, not a fallback. The labelled evaluation set (>= 10 requests, >= 6 images) has no stated path or versioning.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the brief states the degraded path: schema_ok = false, all fields unknown, manual entry of every field, journey continues, with a [D] test. The eval corpus must be committed under a named, versioned path.

findings.title: Model rephrasing of planner explanations adds cost and injection surface for no required outcome
findings.detail: ai/explain.js lets the model rephrase planner-trace explanations, and 'never add facts' is not testable as stated. No RS id requires this feature. It adds a second paid call per plan, and catalog text (an RS-05 injection vector) flows into that prompt.
findings.recommendation: Render explanations deterministically from the trace by default. If rephrasing is kept, make it opt-in and labelled, and cover it with the RS-05 control-run comparison and a check that every number in the output appears in the trace.

findings.title: Idempotency details to pin in design
findings.detail: Reusing an Idempotency-Key with a different body should be refused, not replayed. The research says PayPal-Request-Id must be unique per call type and proposes <operationKey>:<kind>. The brief says PayPal-Request-Id = operation key, which is consistent only if each kind has its own row and key.
findings.recommendation: Record both rules in the design's interface contracts.

findings.title: Design-blocking open questions have workable defaults; record them as decisions
findings.detail: Q1, Q3 and Q6 block design, but the brief already states defaults: A2 single-credential fallback, haiku with a USD 1 ceiling, and A10 polling fallback. Q8 is answered by the goal (English interface).
findings.recommendation: Record the defaults as decisions so design can proceed, and keep Q1/Q3/Q6 open for the user to override.

findings.title: Risk register misses three material risks
findings.detail: Three material risks have no entry. (1) An authorization can expire or pass its honour window while the saga waits for supplier confirmations; the validity periods are unverified (ev:ev-mv16gcdz-01d03c53). (2) Browser installation on judges' clean clones (ARCH-5). (3) node:sqlite is still experimental: it emits an ExperimentalWarning on 22.22 (ev:ev-mv16fndw-01e46e13) and is flagged before 22.13.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the register adds these three risks with likelihood, impact, mitigation and owner. For authorization expiry, the mitigation should re-read expiration_time and void and re-authorize.

findings.title: Upload validation basis and ownership unspecified
findings.detail: RS-39 rejects non-PNG/JPEG/WebP files but does not say whether by declared content type or by file signature, so a declared image/png with arbitrary bytes might pass. The AC also does not assert that only the owning customer can attach an image to a request; RS-27 covers reads only.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when RS-39 specifies magic-byte detection and an owner check, each with an assertion.

findings.title: Credential-per-merchant is unverified, and its single-credential fallback weakens live RS-22
findings.detail: A2 is reasonable but rests on search summaries marked 'verify' (ev:ev-mv16gcdz-01d03c53). I could not check paypal.com either; it is blocked here. A2 implies one buyer approval per supplier order, which the UI must announce before the journey starts. In single-credential mode, the refund of supplier 1 and the capture of supplier 2 hit the same account, so live RS-22 no longer demonstrates cross-merchant compensation.
findings.recommendation: State in A2 that the number of buyer approvals equals the number of supplier orders and is shown up front. Name the RS-18..26 live rows that single-credential mode weakens and label them in the evidence table.

findings.title: Core architecture and the canonical fixture live outside the submission
findings.detail: The Architecture section says 'Modules, data model, contracts, planner and saga are as specified in docs/build/plan.md section 2-6 and are adopted unchanged here'. The RS-FIX-1 table (prices, fees, ready times, compatibility) is not in the brief either: the brief has 0 supplier table rows and goal.md has 5 (ev:ev-mv16g60f-0190c7f8). The submission pins only brief.md, so an approval would vouch for plan.md and goal.md content that is neither pinned nor reviewable through the gate. Several ACs depend on that content: RS-06..11 on the fixture and the planner multiplicity rule; RS-36 on the state tables; RS-20..22 on the saga order. The engine refuses artifact citations outside the submission, which is why plan.md and goal.md are cited here as file evidence.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the resubmission either includes docs/build/plan.md (and the fixture source) as submitted artifacts, or inlines into the brief the RS-FIX-1 table with inventory (ARCH-1), the planner feasibility and multiplicity rules, the four state machines with the derivation table (ARCH-2), and the saga order with claim and void rules (ARCH-3).

findings.title: RS-14 needs a busy timeout: without it the losing process gets 'database is locked', not OUT_OF_STOCK
findings.detail: The brief claims 'WAL + BEGIN IMMEDIATE + CHECK constraints gives serialisable conditional updates sufficient for RS-14'. My two-process race on node:sqlite (ev:ev-mv16fndw-01e46e13) gave these results. With the default busy timeout of 0: one RESERVED, the other 'ERROR database is locked'. With PRAGMA busy_timeout=3000: one RESERVED, the other OUT_OF_STOCK, final reserved = on_hand = 1. The design is feasible, but the claim is incomplete, and RS-14 as written would fail or flake without the timeout.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the brief states the busy-timeout setting (PRAGMA busy_timeout, which works on 22.5+) and maps SQLITE_BUSY after the timeout to a retryable 503 rather than a 500. RS-14 must assert that the loser receives OUT_OF_STOCK, not a lock error.

findings.title: Retention of images and request PII depends on a manual admin reset and is only partly tested
findings.detail: A5 and RS-39 say images are deleted with the request 'or by admin reset after 7 days'. No automatic job is specified, the 7-day rule has no AC, no workflow or route lets a customer delete a request, and the retention of raw_text, extractions and account data is not stated.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the brief specifies an automatic retention sweep (or states that retention is manual-only for the demo and says so in the README), the customer route that deletes a request, and a [D] assertion for the 7-day sweep.

rev-mv1bcexb-01d7960e.summary: Re-review of revision 2 (sub-mv1awqkf-017ea892, brief sha256 f2d88ddf...). I read the brief in full against goal.md and independently re-derived the planner outcomes (ev:ev-mv1b4ffi-01126af0), the rescue-status derivation table (ev:ev-mv1b5tno-019d3877), the AC coverage and goal-id fidelity (ev:ev-mv1b6f7t-016a8217) and the Node 22.5 fallback mechanics (ev:ev-mv1b64bb-01e7637d). All 7 earlier major findings (ARCH-1..6, ARCH-19) and every earlier minor and info finding are resolved. Every one of the 45 required criteria is met and testable. Five new minor findings (ARCH-22..26) are left for the design gate. The Node floor narrowing is acceptable only as recorded: pending the user's answer Q9, with a pass condition kept for the goal's 22.5.

criteria.description: Equivalent Arabic and English requests (RS-FIX-1 wording) yield identical core fields: product type, quantities, capacity, diameter, deadline, budget, max pickups. [D with fake provider; LM with real model over corpus `test/fixtures/extraction/` version EXT-1, equality on normalised fields]
A clear package image yields capacity/diameter specifications carrying `provenance: "image"`. [D fake; LM real]

An ambiguous image yields `unknown` for unreadable fields plus at least one clarification question, and no numeric value absent from the image. Degraded path: when the provider times out, errors, returns schema-invalid output, or is refused by the daily budget or rate limit, the extraction row has `schema_ok = false` and an error code, every field is `unknown`, the response carries `degraded: true`, and the request page shows the labelled notice "Automatic reading unavailable — please enter the details" with a manual field for every core field (provenance `manual`); confirming those fields creates a requirements version and planning proceeds. [D fake incl. faults timeout, invalid_json, schema_invalid; B: test:browser for the notice; LM real]

With budget or deadline missing, `POST /api/plans/:id/approve` and `POST /api/orders/:id/paypal/create` return 409 with a named reason (`MISSING_BUDGET` / `MISSING_DEADLINE`) and no reservation or payment operation is created. [D]

Injection strings in image text and catalog text appear only as data in `fields_json`/catalog; after extraction no permission, amount, supplier, plan version or role differs from the control run; explanations stay template-rendered from planner codes, and when opt-in rephrasing is enabled the same control-run comparison holds and any output containing a number or supplier code absent from the trace is discarded in favour of the template text. [D fake with injection fixtures; LM real]

With RS-FIX-1 and its pinned inventory, the planner returns plan A+B with total 8400 cents (A 4000 + B 4400), 2 pickups, ready 10:30; multiplicity guard: with A's on_hand set to 2 the same planner returns A×2 at 7000 cents with 1 pickup (ev:ev-mv1719y8-011f6742); the oracle property test runs on random catalogs of ≤ 6 offers with on_hand 0–3, so multiplicities above 1 are exercised. [D]

criteria.notes: Independent solver: A+B 8400, 2 pickups, 10:30; with A on_hand 2 it returns Ax2 at 7000 with 1 pickup.

Supplier D's bundle is rejected with code `READY_AFTER_DEADLINE` (ready 11:20 > deadline 11:00). [D]
With the pinned inventory and B removed (on_hand 0 or offer withdrawn; B listed `OUT_OF_STOCK` or withdrawn) the best plan is A+E at 9500 cents (A 4000 + E 5500), 2 pickups, ready 10:40. [D]

criteria.notes: A+E 9500, 2 pickups, 10:40 reproduced.

criteria.description: With the pinned inventory, B removed and budget 9000 cents the planner returns no feasible plan, lists blocking constraints including `OVER_BUDGET`, gives A and E the per-candidate codes `INSUFFICIENT_QTY` and `OVER_BUDGET`, and returns exactly two computed relaxations: budget → 9500 cents yields A+E at 9500 cents, and deadline → 11:20 yields D alone at 8000 cents with 1 pickup; no max-pickups relaxation is emitted because raising max pickups yields no plan (ev:ev-mv1719y8-011f6742, ev:ev-mv171l87-01672a57). [D]
criteria.notes: Reproduced: A and E carry INSUFFICIENT_QTY + OVER_BUDGET; exactly two relaxations (budget 9500 gives A+E 9500; deadline 11:20 gives D 8000, 1 pickup); no max-pickups relaxation.

criteria.description: With the pinned inventory and max pickups = 1 the canonical scenario is infeasible; each compatible, in-time candidate (A, B, E) carries exactly the per-candidate codes `INSUFFICIENT_QTY` (alone it supplies 100 of 200) and `TOO_MANY_PICKUPS` (its cheapest covering combination needs 2 suppliers), while C and D keep their RS-07/RS-08 codes (ev:ev-mv171l87-01672a57). [D]
criteria.notes: Reproduced: A, B, E carry exactly INSUFFICIENT_QTY + TOO_MANY_PICKUPS under the cheapest-covering-combination rule; relaxations TOO_MANY_PICKUPS (A+B 8400) and READY_AFTER_DEADLINE (D 8000) match the brief.

criteria.description: A plan whose cups or lids total < required quantity cannot be produced as feasible, and approval of a tampered plan body is refused with 409. [D]

After the price of an offer used by an approved plan changes, while that supplier's order is not yet `confirmed` and the plan is not `executing`, the approved version becomes `superseded`, totals are recalculated in a new `proposed` version, and reserve/execute on the old version return 409 `PLAN_SUPERSEDED` until the new version is approved; every authorization on the old version ends `voided` (one void provider call each), its reservation is `released` (one ledger row per item), its supplier orders are `cancelled`, and the request shows "Prices changed: review plan vN"; a price change after that supplier confirmed, or after the claim to `executing`, does not supersede the plan (asserted). [D]
evidence: artifact:.eccode/artifacts/architecture/brief.md#State machines (`domain/states.js`; transitions outside these tables are refused and audited)
criteria.notes: Supersession stop point (supplier confirmed or plan executing) is stated and asserted.

criteria.description: Two separate OS processes, each connection with `PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000`, reserve supplier A's last bundle (pinned inventory, on_hand = 1) concurrently against the same SQLite file; exactly one reservation is `active`, the other receives `OUT_OF_STOCK` (not a lock error and not a 500); `reserved <= on_hand` holds; a separate test with `busy_timeout = 0` and a held write lock shows SQLITE_BUSY mapped to 503 `DB_BUSY` with `Retry-After`. [D, multi-process]

An expired reservation is released exactly once: inventory returns to its prior value, the ledger holds one release row, and a second expiry pass is a no-op; an expiry pass run after the execute claim and before the first capture (reservation `consumed`) changes nothing; on expiry before execute every authorization of that plan ends `voided`, the plan is `non_executable` (`RESERVATION_EXPIRED`), and the request shows "Reservation expired — no money was taken; re-plan with current stock". [D]
evidence: artifact:.eccode/artifacts/architecture/brief.md#State machines (`domain/states.js`; transitions outside these tables are refused and audited)
criteria.notes: Expiry touches only active rows, so it is a no-op after the claim consumed the reservation.

criteria.description: Two `reserve` calls with the same `Idempotency-Key` and body return the same reservation id and create no second reservation or ledger row; the same key with a different body returns 422 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED` and changes nothing. [D]

Supplier refusal before the execute claim sets the order to `refused`; every outstanding authorization of that plan version ends `voided`, its reservation is `released`, the plan is `non_executable` (`SUPPLIER_REFUSED`), the rescue status reads `cancelling` while a void is outstanding, the customer request shows the refusal reason with the next step "Review the new plan", and a new plan version is computed excluding that supplier. [D; B: test:browser]

Cancelling on PayPal (cancel URL) leaves that supplier's operation `created` with `buyer_cancelled_at` (no provider authorization exists) or `voided`, no capture call or capture row exists, and `execute` returns 409; the buyer is offered "Try approval again" and "Abandon purchase"; on "Abandon purchase" or reservation expiry every other supplier's outstanding authorization ends `voided`, the reservation is `released`, and the plan is `non_executable` (`PAYMENT_CANCELLED` or `RESERVATION_EXPIRED`). [D fake; LP]
A client-supplied amount/currency/supplier on any payment route is ignored; the PayPal order amount equals the server-approved supplier-order total. [D; LP]

Two server processes on the same SQLite file each receive N = 5 concurrent `execute` requests for the same plan: exactly one `approved → executing` claim commits (conditional UPDATE inside `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`), the other nine return the current state without any provider call, and the fake adapter (state persisted in the same database) records exactly one capture call per supplier order with `PayPal-Request-Id` equal to its deterministic operation key `so:<supplierOrderId>:capture:1`; three repeated hits on the PayPal return URL for one supplier order (refresh/back) produce exactly one authorize call. [D fake, multi-process; LP]

findings.title: The void rule does not cover an operation whose authorize response was lost (status unknown)
findings.detail: The payment-operation table moves an operation approved -> unknown when the authorize call gets no response. The void rule lists operations in created, in approved with no authorize call, in approved with an authorize call still in intent or unknown, in authorization_pending, and in authorized. It does not list an operation whose own status is unknown. An operation with a lost authorize response is therefore in none of these lists when supersession, refusal, abandonment or expiry fires. The reconciler later resolves it to authorized, and nothing persists a void intent for it. The provider authorization stays open until it expires. Derivation row 4 then shows cancelling indefinitely, and row 2 never escalates it. My implementation of the 13-row table returns cancelling for this case even after 2000 minutes (ev:ev-mv1b5tno-019d3877, GAP case). Placement correction 2 meant to close this, but its wording ('approved with an authorize call still in intent or unknown') matches only the restart case, where the operation is still approved.
evidence: artifact:.eccode/artifacts/architecture/brief.md#State machines (`domain/states.js`; transitions outside these tables are refused and audited)
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the design (1) extends the void rule to operations in unknown whose last call is authorize, so they are voided once the reconciler resolves them to authorized, and (2) adds a [D] assertion: lost authorize response, then supersession, then reconciliation gives exactly one void call and the operation ends voided. Optionally, row 2 also escalates an authorized operation of a superseded or non_executable version that has had no void intent for longer than the pending limit.

findings.title: RS-20 forbids any provider call by losing executors, but the saga re-reads expiration_time from the provider before the claim
findings.detail: Saga step 1 revalidates 'a provider expiration_time (re-read from the provider just before the claim)'. That read happens before BEGIN IMMEDIATE, so every one of the 10 concurrent execute requests in RS-20 performs it. RS-20 says the nine losers 'return the current state without any provider call'. As written, the implementation must break one of the two statements.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when saga step 1 and RS-20 agree. Either move the expiration re-read after the claim (by the lease holder, before the first capture; failure then runs the void rule) or narrow RS-20 to 'without any capture, void or refund call' and allow the read-only authorization GETs.

findings.title: NFR1's Node 22.5 branch does not reach child processes spawned by the multi-process tests
findings.detail: If the user answers Q9 by keeping 22.5, NFR1 says every npm script and the README start command pass --experimental-sqlite. RS-14, RS-20 and RS-26 spawn separate Node processes. A child spawned with process.execPath does not inherit execArgv; it does inherit NODE_OPTIONS. Checked on Node 22.22.0: the child's execArgv lacked --experimental-sqlite, while NODE_OPTIONS carrying --experimental-sqlite --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning was inherited and accepted (ev:ev-mv1b64bb-01e7637d). On 22.5-22.12 those children could not load node:sqlite. This only matters under the 22.5 answer.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the 22.5 branch of NFR1 sets the flag through NODE_OPTIONS in the npm scripts (or requires spawned test processes to pass process.execArgv), and states that the multi-process tests are part of the 22.5 pass condition.

findings.title: Authentication contract is missing from the self-contained brief; the webhook route conflicts with the CSRF rule
findings.detail: The architecture names 'auth (scrypt, sessions, CSRF, RBAC default-deny, owner scope)' and RS-27/28/30 depend on sessions. The API contracts, however, list no sign-in, sign-out or session routes, no session lifetime or rotation, no account provisioning (customer self sign-up or seeded demo accounts), and no throttling of sign-in attempts. Throttling matters most for the startup-provided admin password on a publicly reachable demo. The trust-boundary text also requires the CSRF header on 'every non-GET route'. That would block POST /api/webhooks/paypal/:merchantKey, which has no session and is authenticated by signature instead.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the design contracts list the auth routes, session TTL and rotation on sign-in, and how customer and supplier accounts are provisioned. They must also add a sign-in rate limit or lockout with a [D] assertion, and state that the webhook route is CSRF-exempt and authenticated by signature only.

findings.title: Saga lease takeover while the first executor is still inside a capture call is not fenced
findings.detail: The lease is 60 s and renewed per step. No PayPal HTTP timeout is stated, and 'intent treated as unknown' is stated only for startup. A reconciler in a second process that takes over an expired lease 'resumes at the first supplier order that is not captured'. That order is still authorized while the first process waits on its capture call. The deterministic UNIQUE key does not stop a re-send of the same provider_calls row, and the brief itself calls the provider-side PayPal-Request-Id only a backstop with unverified retention. Nothing says that late writes by the old executor are conditional on still holding the lease. The likelihood is low, but the impact is a double capture (RISK-3).
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the design states three things. (1) The PayPal call timeout is well below the lease (for example 20 s against 60 s). (2) On any takeover, every capture call in intent is treated as unknown and resolved by reading provider state before any re-send. (3) Saga writes are conditional on executor_id and lease_until (fencing). RS-26 or RS-20 must also gain an assertion: process 1 stalls mid-capture past the lease, process 2 takes over, and the fake provider records exactly one capture per supplier order.
