findings.title: Reserve idempotency ignores the plan id: a reused key replays another plan's reservation
findings.detail: Interface Contracts > Conventions: the scope is (user id, route template, key) and the body hash is sha256 of the canonical parsed body. For POST /api/plans/:id/reserve the body is always {} and unknown fields are ignored, so a key first used on plan X and then sent to plan Y finds the same (user, '/api/plans/:id/reserve', key, sha256('{}')) row. It replays X's 200/201 response (reservation and orders of X) instead of 422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED. reservations.operation_key 'res:<customerId>:<key>' (003_planning.sql) is UNIQUE per customer as well, so plan Y can never be reserved under that key, and the collision's error is unspecified once the key row is purged. The security reviewer reproduced the replay on the spec's DDL: 'reserve plan 9 with the same key: {status:201, replayed:true, ... planVersionId:7}' (ev:ev-mv1cj3km-010da2d1; their SEC-4, rated minor there). I rate it major because RS-16 requires that reusing a key for a different request change nothing and return 422, and the contract is frozen for parallel implementers. The SPA stores keys per planVersionId, which hides the defect in the UI but not in the API.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the request fingerprint includes the concrete path (or the plan id) as well as the body: either the scope is (user, method + concrete path, key) or the hash covers {planId, body}, and operation_key includes the plan id. The spec must also state the error for an operation-key collision. Add a [D] case to reserve-idempotency.test.js: the same key on a second plan returns 422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED with no reservation, ledger or order rows.

findings.title: Rescue-status derivation is not total: superseded plan awaiting its replan matches no row
findings.detail: P is 'the newest version that is not superseded'. After supersession (Supersession > Effect and Replan), the only version is superseded until the replan stores a new one. Storing it checks offers_hash with up to 3 retries and has no defined outcome once the retries run out. The queue may also wait for the next reconciler tick after a crash. In that state rows 1-4 do not match once the voids are done. Row 5 needs an infeasible latest run, rows 6-12 need P, and row 13 needs no planning run. My derivation probe implements the brief's 13 rows, the spec's ARCH-22 clause and the OQ-D2 row. It confirms RS-36 (i)-(iv) and reports scenario S13 as '<NO ROW MATCHES>' (ev:ev-mv1ciqrf-016a0687). The same probe shows the brief's rows alone also leave OQ-D2's case unmatched, which the spec already patches. deriveRescueStatus's contract returns rule 1..13 with no fallback. GET /api/requests/:id therefore has no defined status in a state RS-32's journey passes through while the SPA polls every 2 s.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the spec defines a total derivation. Add an explicit row, or a definition of P, for 'no current version, replan queued or retries exhausted', with a status from the goal's set or a stated extension and a nextStep (for example WAIT, or REPLAN after the retries run out). Define what happens when the 3 offers_hash retries run out (re-queue or store infeasible). Add a derive.test.js property test: every combination of plan, reservation, operation and fulfilment states reachable through domain/states.js maps to exactly one row and never to undefined.

findings.title: Queued authorize intents have no sender after a crash or a retryable answer; the operation is stranded in 'approved'
findings.detail: The return handler commits 'created -> approved' and queues so:<id>:authorize:1 (started_at NULL) in one transaction. It then runs the call protocol in a later transaction. If the process dies between the two, the call stays queued. Stale-intent recovery matches only 'started_at <= now - 2 x timeout', so it never matches. Reconciler step 6 sends only 'queued void, refund and capture intents'. A repeated return hit answers 303 with no call because the status is no longer 'created'. A 'retryable' answer (401/403/429) also puts the call back to queued. Recovery says it is 're-queued with back-off ... then every tick', but no reconciler step sends authorize. SEC-6 shows that an anonymous webhook flood can induce PayPal 429s on a merchant credential. Consequences: execute returns AUTHORIZATION_PENDING indefinitely. When the void rule fires (expiry, abandon), an 'approved' operation with an authorize call in intent is left 'for later', but nothing resolves it. Row 4 then reports 'cancelling' forever, and row 2 never escalates 'approved' (the probe lists 'approved' among the states that never escalate, scenario S18, ev:ev-mv1ciqrf-016a0687). DELETE /api/requests/:id is refused (PAYMENT_IN_PROGRESS) and admin reset is blocked unless forced.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when, for every call kind, the spec names the component that sends a queued (started_at NULL) or retryable call and when it does so. For authorize, either the reconciler sends it (it is provably unsent), or, if cancel_requested_at is set, the call becomes 'cancelled' and the operation is voided locally. Row 2 must also escalate an operation left in 'approved' with an outstanding authorize call past the unknown limit. Add a [D] test: a fault hook stops the process after the return-handler commit; after a restart and reconcile, exactly one authorize call has been made, or the call is cancelled and the operation 'voided', and the request leaves 'cancelling'.

findings.title: NFR1: on an older Node, npm start fails with 'bad option' before the version gate can name the required version
findings.detail: Deployment: npm start is 'node --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning src/index.js'. In the 22.5 branch, every script also gets '--experimental-sqlite' right after 'node'. Node parses these flags before src/index.js runs. My check ran both command shapes on the older Node binaries on this host (ev:ev-mv1cir59-01e77df9). On v20.20.0 and v21.7.3 the 22.5-branch command exits 9 with 'bad option: --experimental-sqlite' and does not name the required version. The >=22.13-branch command does reach the gate there. However, the Node 20 changelog shows --disable-warning was introduced in 20.11.0, so Node 18 and Node 20.0-20.10 fail the default command the same way. npm only warns on engines. The planned test (test/unit/config/node-version.test.js) unit-tests the gate function on this host's Node 22.22, so it cannot see the defect. NFR1 requires that 'on an older Node npm start exits non-zero with a message naming the required version'.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the start path runs the version gate before any version-specific node flag is parsed. For example: 'start' runs a flag-free 'node scripts/check-node.js' first, or src/index.js re-spawns itself with the flags after the check, or the warning is filtered in code instead of by flag. The same applies to the 22.5 branch. Add a [D] or inspection test that runs the actual npm start command line on an older Node binary when one is available (this host has /opt/node20 and /opt/node21), or at least asserts that the start script begins with a flag-free gate.

findings.title: Anyone can lock any known account (admin included) out of sign-in
findings.detail: Folded in from the security reviewer (.eccode/reviews/drafts/design-security-1.md, SEC-1); I also confirmed it from the spec text. Authentication > Throttle refuses a sign-in 'when the username has >= 5 failures in the last 15 min ... before the password is checked, so the correct password is also refused', and T8 asserts that behaviour. The seed publishes fixed usernames (admin, supplier-a..e, cafe1, cafe2). The security reviewer's executable model printed 'attacker (1 IP, 5 requests): 401 x5 | real admin, other IP, correct password: 429 RATE_LIMITED | after the next 5-guess cycle: 429' (ev:ev-mv1cj3km-010da2d1; spec text quoted in ev:ev-mv1chwnv-0109783d H2). Locking out the suppliers stalls confirmations, so reservations expire and the void rule fires. A live demo can be stalled with 40 requests per 15 minutes.
findings.recommendation: Resolved as the security reviewer states. The hard refusal is keyed on (username, IP) with a per-IP global limit. Across IPs a username gets a progressive delay, or a higher threshold that still checks the password. Failures for unknown usernames are counted the same way, so 429-versus-401 does not enumerate accounts. Username keys are normalised (SEC-9). T8 changes to: '6th attempt from the same IP gives 429; the correct password from another IP gives 200'.

findings.title: One customer can hold every supplier's stock, repeatedly, without paying
findings.detail: Folded in from the security reviewer (SEC-2), and consistent with my reading of Reservation and Authentication > Provisioning. Self-registration is on by default (OQ-D3). Requests can be confirmed manually, which needs no model budget. Seeded on_hand is 1 per supplier, and nothing caps live reservations per customer. One customer can therefore reserve every bundle with fresh Idempotency-Keys and repeat after each 30-minute TTL, while every other customer's reserve fails OUT_OF_STOCK and their plans go non_executable. Reproduced on the spec's DDL: 'attacker reserves each supplier bundle: 201 x5 | live reservations held: 5 | victim reserve: 409 OUT_OF_STOCK' (ev:ev-mv1cj3km-010da2d1; spec text in ev:ev-mv1chwnv-0109783d H6).
findings.recommendation: Resolved as the security reviewer states. Add a per-customer cap on live reservations (default 1, for example RS_MAX_LIVE_RESERVATIONS_PER_CUSTOMER), refused with a catalogued 409 or 429 code, and a per-customer daily limit on request creation. Assert both in an API test. Optionally, shorten the TTL until the first PayPal approval.

findings.title: A loopback PayPal stub under npm start is labelled 'PayPal Sandbox', not 'Simulated' (RS-34)
findings.detail: Folded in from the security reviewer (SEC-3). T18 and the wire mapping accept RS_PAYPAL_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:<port> and a loopback approval host for the paypal-sandbox adapter, with no restriction to tests. Under npm start that produces provider 'paypal-sandbox', simulated:false and sandbox:true, the 'PayPal Sandbox — no real money' badge and no Simulated banner, for a flow that is simulated. RS-34 requires everything that is not real to be labelled. The labelling test asserts the Sandbox labels against this stub. Evidence: spec text quoted in ev:ev-mv1chwnv-0109783d (H5).
findings.recommendation: Resolved when a loopback PayPal base URL and approval host are accepted only under RS_TEST_OFFLINE=1 or RS_TEST_HOOKS=1, and npm start refuses them at startup. The alternative is that loopback mode is labelled simulated:true and sandbox:false, shows the Simulated banner and uses a distinct badge. Either way, add a config test and a labelling test for each case.

findings.title: OQ-D2 default labels a partially refunded executed plan 'cancelled'
findings.detail: With admin refund_order on one supplier's order of an executed plan and the other order collected, the OQ-D2 row returns 'cancelled' (probe S15, ev:ev-mv1ciqrf-016a0687). The buyer did receive and pay for part of the plan, so the aggregate misstates it. A related transient case: reserve losing the race gives 'cancelled' until the replan lands (S20).
findings.recommendation: Resolved when OQ-D2's row gives a state that does not claim the whole purchase was cancelled. For example, keep 'collected' or 'purchase_confirmed' with a message naming the refunded order, or use an explicitly named extension. The derive test should assert it.

findings.title: A void rejected because the authorization was captured is recorded as void_failed while money is captured
findings.detail: Void rule step 6: 'rejected -> read the authorization: VOIDED -> voided, else keep authorized with void_failed = 1'. If the read shows CAPTURED (a late capture from a fenced or stalled sender landed after a read showed none; see SEC-18), the operation still says 'authorized' although the buyer was charged. refund_order only accepts 'captured' under an 'executed' plan, so no tool can refund it. The derivation escalates it (row 2), so it is not silent, but it is stranded.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when a void-result read that shows CAPTURED moves the operation to 'captured' and the compensating-plan refund hook queues so:<id>:refund:1, with a fake-adapter test (capture applied after the void intent).

findings.title: Saga step 3 behaviour for an operation in capture_pending or unknown after takeover is not stated
findings.detail: A pause sets lease_until = now, so reconciler step 5 takes the plan over on every tick (the epoch grows) and resumes 'for the first operation not captured'. That operation is the capture_pending or unknown one. The start CAS refuses (the call is not a fresh intent), so nothing is double-sent, but the spec does not say that step 3 must re-pause without sending, nor that takeover should skip plans whose only open item is pending or unknown.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when step 3 states that an operation in capture_pending or unknown pauses the saga without a send, and the reconciler takes over a paused plan only once that operation is resolved. RS-22's PENDING case should assert that the epoch does not grow per tick.

findings.title: RS-20 test attributes provider calls by pid, which cannot see losers in the winner's process
findings.detail: rs20-two-process-execute asserts 'zero provider calls attributed to the losers' pids'. Four of the nine losers run in the winner's process, so a stray call from one of them would be counted as the winner's.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the test also asserts the exact total of fake_paypal_calls for the run: N getAuthorization reads plus N captures, and nothing else.

findings.title: Traceability gaps: RS-36 lacks its [I] inspection; RS-03's [D] ambiguous-image half names no test
findings.detail: The traceability check (ev:ev-mv1cik0q-01d57f54) finds all 45 ids exactly once, each with a section and a test. It warns that RS-36's row omits the brief's [I] tag. RS-03's row lists degraded-path faults for [D] but not the ambiguous-image assertion, which test/eval/extraction-fake.test.js would cover.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the RS-36 row names its inspection and the RS-03 row names the [D] ambiguous-image test.

findings.title: Per-customer rate limit check and insert are not stated to be atomic across processes
findings.detail: Runtime controls step 1 counts rate_events and then inserts, but only the budget step says 'in one transaction'. Two processes can each count 9 and both insert.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the rate check and insert run in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction, as the budget step does.

findings.title: Compensated plans leave supplier orders 'confirmed'
findings.detail: Fulfilment allows -> cancelled only before the claim, so after CAPTURE_FAILED or post-claim AUTHORIZATION_EXPIRED the orders stay 'confirmed' and the supplier dashboard still shows a live order.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the supplier and customer views derive a 'cancelled (payment failed)' presentation for orders of a non_executable plan, or the fulfilment machine adds the edge (a brief change to raise with the orchestrator).

findings.title: Model spend stored as REAL dollars

findings.recommendation: Resolved when spend is stored as INTEGER micro-dollars (or the comparison is stated with a fixed rounding), with the NFR6 boundary case asserted.

findings.title: Wire schema acceptance by the CLI --json-schema and the API is verified only at the first live run
findings.detail: I confirmed that every pinned flag exists (ev:ev-mv1cirha-01fe9dfc) and re-ran the designer's stream-json constraint probe (ev:ev-mv1citom-01b59d5c). Whether $defs/$ref and anyOf-with-null schemas are accepted is not exercised offline, and a rejection would send every live extraction to the degraded path.

findings.title: Fake approval page CSP form-action 'self' blocks the approve/cancel redirect to the app: [B] payment journeys cannot complete
findings.detail:
Revision 2 adds a contract for the fake approval listener (SEC-12). GET /fake-paypal/checkout/:id is served with CSP "default-src 'none'; style-src 'self'; form-action 'self'", and the listener 'applies the same security headers ... as the app', whose CSP also ends in form-action 'self'. POST .../approve answers 303 to the stored return_url on http://localhost:<port> (the app), and POST .../cancel answers 303 to the cancel_url. Chromium enforces form-action across the redirect chain of a form submission. I reproduced the spec's page with Playwright's Chromium (ev:ev-mv1dhs2e-012e67d4):
- (A) the spec's CSP: the browser stays on the fake page with 'Refused to send form data ... violates the following Content Security Policy directive', and the return route is never hit.
- (B) form-action 'self' plus the app origin: the browser reaches the return route with the SameSite=Lax session cookie.
- (C) no CSP: same as (B).
- (D) control: a Strict cookie is not sent, so the return really is cross-site, which is what RS-31 requires.
As specified, test/browser/journey-happy (RS-31(a)), journey-replacement (RS-32(a)) and the NFR2 keyboard-only happy path cannot get past the first PayPal approval.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when every Content-Security-Policy header the fake approval listener sends either lists the app's return origin in form-action (form-action 'self' <RS_PUBLIC_URL origin>) or omits form-action. That includes the inherited app security headers, because two CSP headers are both enforced. The same applies to the test helper paypal-stub's approval page. Test: a [B] assertion in journey-happy that the approve and cancel clicks land on /api/paypal/return and /api/paypal/cancel with the session (it would have caught this), plus a [D] header test that pins the listener's CSP value.

resolvedFindings.resolution: Scope (user, key) with a fingerprint over method, concrete path and body; reservations.idempotency_key UNIQUE per customer; operation_key carries the plan id; collisions mapped explicitly; [D] cases include the second plan before and after purge. On the revised DDL the same customer's key on plan 2 is refused by UNIQUE (customer_id, idempotency_key) with no idempotency_keys row present, another customer may reuse the text, and the key PK refuses a second fingerprint.

The derivation is total: row 4a (replanning) for a queued re-plan, a re-plan queue that never drops entries after the retries run out, and a defensive row 14 with a property test. My own implementation of the revised table gives S13/S13b 'replanning', S15 'collected', S15b 'cancelled', S15c (admin refund unknown) 'refunding', and RS-36 (i)-(iv) unchanged. Exhaustive enumeration of 493,074 abstract states reaches row 14 only in 326 unreachable states: a feasible run with no version, or an unknown whose prev_status cannot occur under P's status.

The Sender table names who sends each queued or retryable call kind. A queued authorize is sent by reconciler step 6, or cancelled with the operation voided locally once cancellation is requested. Row 2(a) escalates 'approved' with an outstanding authorize after the unknown limit, and the return-crash integration test covers it. In my derivation probe, S18 ends 'cancelled' (not stuck in cancelling), while S18b (started authorize unknown, 20 min) and S18c (429 re-queued, 20 min) reach failed_needs_attention.

Every flagged script begins with the flag-free 'node scripts/check-node.cjs &&'. I ran the spec's start line verbatim through /bin/sh and through 'npm run start'. On Node 20.20 and 21.7 it exits 1 with 'RescueStock needs Node >= 22.13 (found ...)', and the 22.5-branch line names 22.5. On 22.22 the app starts. Every flagged script in the block carries the gate prefix.

The hard 429 is keyed on (normalised username, IP), 5 per 15 min, plus 20 per IP. Across IPs a username gets only a 1-10 s delay, and the password is still checked. Unknown usernames are counted alike, and T8 is rewritten. On the revised login_failures schema, five failures from the attacker IP reach the pair limit for that IP only: the pair on another IP is 0 and the cross-IP total stays below the delay threshold.

There is a live-reservation cap (default 1) checked inside the reserve BEGIN IMMEDIATE, giving 409 RESERVATION_LIMIT, and 10 requests per customer per day with count and insert atomic, both asserted in abuse-limits.test.js. Two OS processes reserving two different plans for the same customer give exactly RESERVED + RESERVATION_LIMIT. The RS-32 sequence (void-rule release, then replacement reserve) passes under the cap.

Loopback PayPal and Anthropic base URLs, and a loopback approval host, are accepted only with RS_TEST_OFFLINE=1, which sets labels.testMode and shows the 'Test mode — local stubs, nothing is real' banner. Startup refuses them otherwise, and T18 and the RS-34 traceability name the config and labelling tests for both cases. This is a text-level fix, checked against the spec's Conventions, Security and Deployment sections and the traceability run.

findings.title: Concurrent start on a fresh database fails: PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL throws SQLITE_BUSY despite busy_timeout
findings.detail:
src/db/connection.js sets `PRAGMA busy_timeout` and then `PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL` (L29-L30). When several processes open a new database file at the same time, SQLite can return SQLITE_BUSY for the journal-mode switch without calling the busy handler. It does this when waiting could deadlock: one connection holds a shared lock and needs an exclusive one while another holds or waits for a write lock.
- In my phase run of `npm test`, 'NFR1: two processes starting at the same time apply each migration exactly once and both succeed' failed: a child exited with 'Error: database is locked' at openDb, connection.js:30 (ev:ev-mv1h5bbh-010aae6e, 363/364).
- The reproduction ran that test 10 times in isolation; 1 failed with the same error (ev:ev-mv1h6fnx-0154466d).
b1's criterion requires that 'a second process starting at the same time skips applied versions', and the spec calls migrations multi-process safe. The later multi-process tests (rs14, rs20, rs26, lease-takeover, return-crash), and any two-server deployment, start processes on one fresh file and would inherit the race as flaky failures or startup crashes. The delivery lead's 364/364 run and my b1/b3 runs passing does not contradict this: the failure is intermittent.
findings.recommendation:
Owner: b1-foundation-core (backend-engineer), src/db/connection.js.
Fix: openDb retries the journal-mode switch, and any other SQLITE_BUSY raised while opening, with a short bounded back-off up to the busy timeout, then gives a clear error. A synchronous sleep such as Atomics.wait on a SharedArrayBuffer is fine.
Add a regression test (or raise the existing one to at least 25 rounds of 3 processes) named with its id.
Resolved when the reviewer's reruns pass: `npm test` and `node .eccode/drafts/tr-phb-migrate-race.mjs 20` with 0 failures.
If a retry does not remove the failures, dispatch learning-debugger on PB-1 to find the root cause.

findings.title: Residual: tie-laden catalogs beyond version one's reachable catalog still reach PLANNER_LIMIT, bounded at about 0.1-0.3 s per call
findings.detail:
My probe (ev:ev-mv1ju48g-01caf1f8) measured three catalog kinds:
- Seeded products, which is all that PATCH can produce: 1500 adversarial calls, 0 refusals, worst 96 ms.
- C confirmed compatible: 0.13 % refusals, worst refused call 127 ms.
- 12 tie-priced offers: 9.4 % refusals, worst 291 ms.
No version-one route can produce the last two. Products and offers come from the seed, and a PATCH only versions the existing offer of an existing product. No route writes compatibility rows. Random-priced 12-offer catalogs pass (the engineer's 150-catalog test, and the NFR5 generator).
My previous resolution condition asked for exact and fast results up to 12 offers. That holds for random prices but not for adversarial ties at 12 offers. I downgrade the remainder from major to minor for three reasons: it is unreachable through version one's API (verified); the cap bounds each call (at most about 0.3 s measured); and c2's typed 422 (FU-1) and per-customer planning rate limit (FU-8) plus RISK-19 cover it if the catalog ever grows.
findings.recommendation: Owners: c2-requests-plans-view (FU-1: PLANNER_LIMIT mapped to a typed 422; FU-8: per-customer planning rate limit, which f1 applies to re-plan drains), and the orchestrator (RISK-19). Any future route that creates offers or compatibility rows must first bring the planner to exact and fast on that larger envelope (for example an integer DP over coverage) or cap the catalog. Resolved when FU-1 and FU-8 are proven in phase C and RISK-19 is either closed or carries this condition.

findings.title: Two canonicalJson implementations; only the HTTP one has a depth limit
findings.detail: src/http/body.js exports a depth-limited canonicalJson (TypeError above 32 levels). src/domain/canonical.js exports a different recursive canonicalJson (used for planHash, offersHash and fingerprints per its header). It has cycle and type checks but no depth limit, and it encodes -0 as 0 while the HTTP one uses JSON.stringify. Neither has a caller in src/ yet. Request bodies cannot exceed 32 levels because readJsonBody refuses them first; my probe confirms the domain encoder handles that deepest accepted body (ev:ev-mv1jyx54-01238917).
findings.recommendation: c-phase route tasks (idempotency fingerprints, planHash) should use one canonical encoder, so the same body cannot produce two different fingerprints, and should only feed it values that passed readJsonBody's depth limit. No change needed in phase B.

resolvedFindings.resolution: The per-offer DFS is replaced by an exact subset search (search.js). It agrees with my brute force on 2 x 3000 random catalogs and with the frozen reference on 1497 medium catalogs, on full output. The security sweep passes: the stock-100, 10,000-cup case gives A in 0.1 ms, worst 38 ms. A named timing test was added (planner-sec-b1.test.js). On every catalog version one can produce, adversarial ties never reach the cap. The residual beyond version one's reachable envelope is tracked as SEC-B-1R (minor), RISK-19, FU-1 and FU-8.

openDb sets PRAGMA recursive_triggers = ON. The security reviewer's probe on the final tree shows INSERT OR REPLACE and REPLACE INTO refused for audit_events and inventory_ledger, with plain appends still allowed. SEC-B-2 tests were added to triggers.test.js.

readJsonBody refuses JSON nested deeper than 32 levels with 422 VALIDATION_FAILED, using a non-recursive text scan before JSON.parse. The HTTP canonicalJson stays recursive but refuses depth above 32 with TypeError, so it cannot overflow the stack.
My independent probe passes:
- 20,000-deep and 33-deep text is refused, and 32 levels are accepted.
- Brackets inside strings are ignored.
- canonicalJson throws TypeError on 20,000-deep objects and arrays.
The hardening tests pass 7/7. The security reviewer's HTTP probe (ev-mv1jrhzy-0128826d) exits 1 only on its obsolete expectation that canonicalJson throws RangeError; that is consistent with the fix, but I do not cite it because it failed.
Recorded as FU-10 for c6: the rs14-db-busy test starts the server before the lock holder takes BEGIN IMMEDIATE.

The server uses connectionsCheckingInterval 1000 and maxConnections 512, and answers timeouts with 408. In the slowloris probe, slow-header connections close at 10-11 s and slow bodies at 30 s, all with 408. The SEC-B-4 hardening tests pass.

- SEC-B-6 (lockfile): decision FU-12.

ho-mv1hk3zz-01649535.completedWork: REWORK after phase B review rev-mv1hc5zg-01a3fc75. PB-1 (blocking), root cause: on a fresh database file, PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL needs an exclusive lock. When another process holds or awaits a write lock while this connection holds a shared one, waiting could deadlock, so SQLite returns SQLITE_BUSY immediately and never calls the busy handler, so busy_timeout does not help. Reproduced with the reviewer's script (ev:ev-mv1hf138-016b38f3: 3 of 40 sequential runs failed with 'database is locked'; the script always exits 0, so the counts are the result) and with a minimal probe (.eccode/drafts/b1-pb1-probe.mjs, error code 5 from the WAL switch, about 1 in 180 opens). Fix in src/db/connection.js: openDb reads the journal mode first and switches only when the file is not WAL, and both that step and the later pragmas run under retryWhileBusy, a bounded back-off (2 ms doubling to 50 ms with jitter) on SQLITE_BUSY/LOCKED up to max(busyTimeoutMs, 1000 ms), after which the busy error is rethrown; the handle is closed on failure. New test/unit/db/open-race.test.js (all named PB-1): retry unit tests, bounded give-up against a real lock-holder process, success when the holder releases, and a stress of 25 rounds x 4 processes on a fresh file. PB-1 (blocking), root cause: on a fresh database file, PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL needs an exclusive lock. ho-mv1jewhq-01c5bca8.completedWork: Algorithm (new src/domain/search.js, used by planner.js): the search enumerates offer SUBSETS within the pickup cap, smallest first, and solves each subset's covering problem exactly by bounded depth-first search. Pickups, plan-ready time and the supplier-code string depend on the subset alone, so inside a subset only total and vector matter. Pruning is valid and exact: (1) only irredundant plans are enumerated (the optimum is always irredundant: dropping a bundle never raises total, pickups or ready time and gives a smaller vector; the forced offer of a cheapest-cover query is exempt); (2) multiplicities are looped only inside the window [kLo, kHi] that the remaining demand allows; (3) a fractional-knapsack lower bound per dimension (mandatory later bundles, prep fees of unused suppliers, tax-rate scaling less one cent of rounding per touched order) cuts subtrees above the budget or the K-th best plan; (4) ascending canonical vector order lets a subtree that can only tie the K-th best of the same subset be cut, which removes equal-cost plateaus; (5) when no supplier has two members, a dominance table keyed by (position, cups, lids) keeps the K cheapest prefixes per state. Subsets are pre-filtered by a cheap root bound (cover floor plus prep sums). For infeasible requests the cheapest unconstrained cover answers every offer it uses, and any other offer is searched with that cover plus one bundle as its starting incumbent. Results: reproduction (stock 100, 10,000 cups, budget USD 100,000, maxPickups 5) now returns A at 301,000 cents in 0.1 ms, same as maxPickups 1. Sweep: 5,400 inputs, no PLANNER_LIMIT, worst single call 21.5 ms (was 237-305 ms with refusals). Stress (draft b2-planner-stress.mjs): 8,000 seeded-shape inputs with availability up to 100,000, quantities up to 100,000, differing cup/lid quantities and tax: worst 9.7 ms, no limit; 3,000 random-priced 12-offer catalogs: worst 36 ms; 3,000 catalogs with several offers per supplier: worst 23 ms. Tests added: planner-oracle.property.test.js gains (a) brute-force oracle on larger stock (availability up to 7, 100 catalogs), (b) tie-heavy catalogs against the oracle (equal prices, prep fees, ready times, several offers per supplier, 120 catalogs), (c) identical tied offers of one supplier, (d) 250 medium catalogs (availability up to 12, up to 6 offers, quantities up to 3000) against the frozen slow exact reference test/unit/domain/helpers/reference-planner.js, comparing the whole output; planner-fixture.test.js replaces the old absurd-input test with 'SEC-B-1: huge stock and quantity are solved exactly' (12 offers of single cups, 100,000 each, solved in well under 1 s) and a guard test of the node cap through search(..., {maxNodes}); test/timing/planner-sec-b1.test.js has the named test, a 1,008-call grid over the seeded shape (stock 1..100,000, quantity 100..100,000, no PLANNER_LIMIT, each < 100 ms, p95 < 20 ms) and 150 random 12-offer catalogs (each < 250 ms). A mutation (pruning ties across different subsets) was caught by the reference comparison and reverted. The earlier suites (RS-06..RS-11, 500-catalog oracle property, derive totality, states, money, time, explain, NFR5) pass unchanged.
remainingIssues: PLANNER_LIMIT (2,000,000 nodes per search, about 150 ms) is still a real guard, not an unreachable one. It is not reached by the seeded catalog shape, by random-priced catalogs of up to 12 offers, or by catalogs with several offers per supplier within the API ranges (evidence above). It CAN still be reached, and calls can take 150-400 ms (up to about 800 ms when several searches hit it), by deliberately tie-laden catalogs: several suppliers whose bundles of different size cost the same per bundle, quantity of about 50,000 or more, and especially a non-zero tax rate (rounding noise defeats tie pruning); and by catalogs whose bundles hold different numbers of cups and lids (not reachable through the API, which only seeds equal counts) at quantity 100,000. A supplier can set equal prices through PATCH, so this is reachable in principle; exactness for those needs an integer DP over coverage that I did not build in this round. Recommended in c2 regardless: map PlannerLimitError (RangeError, code PLANNER_LIMIT) to a typed 422/503, and add the per-customer rate limit on POST /api/requests/:id/plan and on re-plan drains that the security draft asks for (item 3 of its resolution).

RISK-12.title: Sandbox webhooks unreachable in the demo (no public URL)
RISK-12.mitigation: Signature verification path tested with the fake adapter and recorded Sandbox payloads; polling fallback for provider order state (A10, Q6)

RISK-13.title: PayPal authorization expires or passes its honour window while the saga waits for supplier confirmations (validity periods unverified)
RISK-13.mitigation: Re-read expiration_time at revalidation with a 10-minute margin; expired authorization voided and treated like DENIED (void rule, buyer re-approves under a new plan version); 30-minute reservation TTL bounds the wait; fake adapter models expiry

RISK-14.title: Playwright browser download on clean clones is network beyond npm and may fail for judges
RISK-14.mitigation: Browser suites only under npm run test:browser (dec-mv16pz32-013c4cd1); npm test never launches a browser (NFR1/NFR3 ACs); README documents the one-time npx playwright install chromium

RISK-15.title: node:sqlite is experimental: flagged before Node 22.13, ExperimentalWarning on 22.22, API may change
RISK-15.mitigation: Node floor 22.13 or later (dec-mv16pyxx-01bad0bf) with engines field and startup check; --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning; PRAGMA busy_timeout instead of the 22.16-only constructor option; thin db/ wrapper; residual: API churn in future Node versions

RISK-16.title: Session lost on the cross-site PayPal return (SameSite=Strict inherited from Groundwork) breaks authorization only against the real Sandbox
RISK-16.mitigation: Session cookie SameSite=Lax; owner-checked idempotent return handler; fake approval page served from a different site in test:browser; RS-31/32 (b) live Sandbox variants

RISK-17.title: Runtime model spend abuse (looping extract or upload) billed to the user's account
RISK-17.mitigation: Daily model budget RS_MODEL_DAILY_BUDGET_USD, per-customer rate limit of 10 calls per 10 minutes counted in SQLite, per-call cap; asserted deterministically in NFR6

RISK-18.title: Single-credential Sandbox mode makes live RS-19/20/22/23/24 evidence weaker than claimed
RISK-18.mitigation: Merchant mode recorded in every live report; weakened rows labelled in the evidence table (A2); per-supplier credentials requested from the user (Q1)

RISK-19.title: Planner node cap reachable by deliberately tie-laden supplier catalogs (SEC-B-1 residual)
RISK-19.mitigation: c2 maps PlannerLimitError to a typed 422 (FU-1) and adds a per-customer planning rate limit; an integer DP over coverage would remove the cap (not built in version one)

dec-mv15p9bp-01586238.title: Workflow level
dec-mv15p9bp-01586238.rationale: Payments (PayPal authorize/capture/void/refund), authentication, inventory invariants and AI extraction change trust boundaries; orchestrate skill section 1 routes such work to the full delivery with the security reviewer on the phases that touch the boundary.

dec-mv16pyxx-01bad0bf.title: Node version
dec-mv16pyxx-01bad0bf.rationale: ARCH-5: node:sqlite is behind --experimental-sqlite on 22.5-22.12 per the reviewer; the build host runs 22.22. Simpler than a flag in every script.

dec-mv16pz0g-01d5c4c2.title: Q1/Q3/Q4/Q6/Q8 defaults
dec-mv16pz0g-01d5c4c2.decision: Q1: one Sandbox credential set per supplier when supplied, the DEFAULT set otherwise (labelled). Q3: Claude CLI route, haiku for extraction, ceiling USD 5 for the live model suite. Q4: examples/rescuestock stays in this repository. Q6: polling reconciler is the primary path; webhooks verified when a public URL exists. Q8: English UI with dir=auto on text inputs so Arabic renders right-to-left.
dec-mv16pz0g-01d5c4c2.rationale: ARCH-15: reversible defaults so design can proceed; listed for the user, who has not answered yet.

dec-mv16pz32-013c4cd1.title: Test script layout
dec-mv16pz32-013c4cd1.decision: npm test = offline node --test (unit, API, integration with real SQLite); npm run test:browser = Playwright journeys with a documented browser install; test:live-model and test:live-paypal are separate and opt-in by env flag
dec-mv16pz32-013c4cd1.rationale: ARCH-5 and NFR1: a clean clone must pass npm test with no network beyond npm.

dec-mv1e2i2t-0113385a.title: OQ-D6: rescue status set gains 'replanning'
dec-mv1e2i2t-0113385a.decision: Adopt the design's row 4a: a request whose approved plan was superseded and whose re-plan is still queued reads 'replanning' (goal.md's status set is extended by one value).
dec-mv1e2i2t-0113385a.rationale: The reviewer showed the brief's derivation table had no row for this reachable state (RS-32 passes through it while the page polls); the alternative, folding it into 'plan_found', would misstate that no plan is currently proposed. Orchestrator default, reversible by the user; recorded as the designer's open question OQ-D6, decision requested.
dec-mv1e2i2t-0113385a.alternatives: fold into plan_found; show the old plan as superseded with no status change

dec-mv1e2i5k-01a1bebb.title: OQ-D7: per-customer daily model share defaults to 0.2
dec-mv1e2i5k-01a1bebb.decision: Production default RS_MODEL_CUSTOMER_DAILY_SHARE=0.2 of the daily model budget per customer (concurrency 1 per customer); the NFR6 evidence runs with the share pinned to 1 and says so; the user may change both with the Q10 answer (daily budget, default USD 1.00).
dec-mv1e2i5k-01a1bebb.rationale: Security finding SEC-10: a shared daily budget lets a few customers exhaust extraction for everyone. The reviewer (F-TR-18) noted NFR6's stated configuration refuses the first call under 0.2, so the test pins the share to 1 and the acceptance report must state it. Orchestrator default, reversible.
dec-mv1e2i5k-01a1bebb.alternatives: share off (SEC-10 unmitigated); share 1 everywhere (no per-customer protection)

dec-mv1fgdkd-01182466.title: Runtime budget: phase B proceeds within the current 480-minute limit; raise-or-descope decision requested from the user before phase C
dec-mv1fgdkd-01182466.decision: Phase B (4 tasks, ~40-60 recorded minutes) starts now under the existing limit; no implementer dispatch for phase C or later is made until the user has either raised limits.maxRuntimeMinutes in .eccode/config.json or accepted the delivery lead's descoping order (plan.md). The engine's BUDGET_EXCEEDED refusal remains the hard stop.
dec-mv1fgdkd-01182466.rationale: Plan review F-PL-2 asked for the decision before the first phase-B dispatch; the user is not available in this session and phase B fits under either outcome, so waiting would spend wall-clock time without protecting the budget. Orchestrator decision, reversible; the user's choice is still requested and recorded when it arrives.
dec-mv1fgdkd-01182466.alternatives: block all implementation until the user answers; descope now without the user

dec-mv1jb1w1-014069b1.title: Toolkit version checkpoint: 0.3.2 adopted for the rest of the pilot
dec-mv1jb1w1-014069b1.decision: From phase B's third review iteration on, the pilot runs ECCode 0.3.2 (merge cdf515f): TK-1 (phase artifacts union across completions) and TK-2 (test suite isolates shared memory), both found by this pilot, repaired on eccode/phase-artifacts-union with failing-first regression tests and an independent review that reproduced the defects and ran adversarial probes. The guard script is unchanged between 0.3.1 and 0.3.2.
dec-mv1jb1w1-014069b1.rationale: The readiness rule: a mid-pilot repair goes on a separate branch with a regression test, independent review and an explicit version checkpoint; never hot-patched. Without TK-1 every later phase resubmission after a rework would silently shrink its review set.
dec-mv1jb1w1-014069b1.alternatives: stay on 0.3.1 and have the delivery lead name every file by hand at each resubmission

dec-mv1jopyn-01ba1096.title: FU-8: error catalog gains details.limit = plan for the per-customer planning rate limit
dec-mv1jopyn-01ba1096.decision: The 429 RATE_LIMITED envelope may carry details.limit = 'plan' (alongside the existing limit names) when a customer exceeds the per-customer planning rate; c2 implements and tests it.
dec-mv1jopyn-01ba1096.rationale: Mitigation for RISK-19 (SEC-B-1 residual) without changing routes or status codes; a new enumerated value in an existing field is the smallest contract change.
dec-mv1jopyn-01ba1096.alternatives: reuse the general limit name and lose the ability to tell planning throttles apart in the UI

dec-mv1joq3i-01180c65.title: FU-12: commit a package-lock.json
dec-mv1joq3i-01180c65.decision: The repository commits package-lock.json generated by npm install (one devDependency, @playwright/test 1.56.1); the devops task that owns the environment template (g2) adds it and the package scan asserts it is present and matches package.json.
dec-mv1joq3i-01180c65.rationale: SEC-B-6: integrity hashes for the single devDependency cost nothing and the clean-checkout check already runs npm install; zero runtime dependencies is unchanged.
